Description: A vector from the origin ends at (3, 4). The target subspace is the horizontal axis.
The bars at components 1, 2 and 3 have heights 5, 3 and 1.
Two long horizontal bands have the same x coordinates. Class A lies just above zero on feature 2 and B just below it.
Contours are elongated along parameter 1. Successive steps cross the valley floor along parameter 2.
At FPR 0.02, detectors A and B reach recall 0.45 and 0.54 respectively. A leads at higher false-positive rates.
The top 4 operating point has recall 0.75 and precision 0.75. The top 6 point has the same recall and precision 0.50.
At forecast 0.50, group A has observed frequency 0.62 and group B has 0.38. The groups have equal size in each bin.
The gradient arrow ends at (3, 4). A dashed circle marks the norm limit 2.
Rows and columns are zero-indexed. Nonzero weights by row are [1], [0.2, 0.8], [0.1, 0.2, 0.45, 0.25], and [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], all starting in column 0.
Tokens A, B, C and D have probabilities 0.55, 0.25, 0.15 and 0.05.
The roof rises at 2 TFLOP/s per FLOP/byte until reaching a flat ceiling of 200 TFLOP/s.
Through the same stationary point, the loss rises in both directions along line A and falls in both directions along line B.
For targets 0, 0 and 9, the squared-error curve has its minimum at prediction 3 and the absolute-error curve at 0.
Training and deployment both occupy A, B and C. Region D has positive deployment mass and zero training mass.
Within each of the triples ABC and DEF every pair has been compared. No edge connects the two triples.
With unit population standard deviation, standard error falls from 0.25 at 16 independent observations to 0.125 at 64.
Both RBF curves start at similarity 1. Curve B drops more steeply with distance than curve A.
Solid unit vectors q and k are 60 degrees apart. Both dashed vectors are rotated a further 90 degrees.
Two lines show a clean sinusoid and its corruption. The noisy signal equals 0.8 times the clean signal plus 0.6 times standard Gaussian noise.
The constant-compute curve goes through 2 billion parameters with 20 billion tokens and 4 billion parameters with 10 billion tokens.
A transition yields reward 1. At the nonterminal next state, the two available actions have Q estimates of 4 and 2.
Model A has cost 2 and quality 0.78, B has cost 4 and quality 0.85, and C has cost 5 and quality 0.80. All meet the latency limit.
